findings.title: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES only applied when a search query is entered
findings.body: `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` (`is_segment`, `project_id`, `received`) is checked only in the `.filter()` that runs after the `if (!searchQuery.trim()) return sorted;` early return. With an empty search box, which is the default, the hidden attributes are still shown. They disappear as soon as the user types something, so the list changes inconsistently. The hidden-attribute filter needs to run before the early return so it applies in both cases.

findings.title: Error timestamps (seconds) are compared against replay event timestamps (milliseconds)
findings.body: `gen_request_data` compares `error_events[i]["timestamp"]` with `event.get("timestamp", 0)`. Error timestamps come from the nodestore event payload and are float seconds (~1.7e9). Replay recording events (rrweb) carry millisecond timestamps (~1.7e12). Every error is therefore treated as earlier than the first replay event, and all errors are emitted at the start of the log instead of interleaved chronologically. The unit tests hide this because they use seconds for both sides (`now.timestamp()`, 1.5/3.0). The error timestamp should be converted to ms, or the replay timestamp to seconds, before comparing and before formatting the log line.

findings.title: Snuba replay query runs even when error context is disabled
findings.body: `query_replay_instance` and `process_raw_response` are executed unconditionally to obtain `error_ids`. The `enable_error_context=false` check is only evaluated afterwards, so the result is discarded. A disabled request still pays for an extra Snuba query. Check the flag first and skip the query.

findings.title: zip(error_ids, events.values()) can pair IDs with the wrong events
findings.body: `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a dict keyed by node id. Depending on the backend, it may omit missing keys or not preserve request order. Zipping `error_ids` with `events.values()` can then attach the wrong event id to an event, or shift the pairing after a missing node. Iterate over the `node_ids` and look each one up in the returned dict, or build the id mapping explicitly.

findings.title: Analytics event recorded before the feature-flag check
findings.body: `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` fires before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` feature check and before any payload validation. Requests from organizations without the feature, which get a 404, still emit the event. That inflates usage numbers for a feature that is not enabled. Move the call after the feature gate, or after validation, so only real attempts are counted.

findings.title: age/timestamp exclusivity check uses truthiness and does not require either field
findings.body: `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` test `self.initial_data.get("age")` and `get("timestamp")` for truthiness. A report with `age: 0` or `timestamp: 0` (both valid) passes alongside the other field, so the 'mixed' check is bypassed. Both fields are also `required=False`, and field-level validators only run when the field is present. A report with neither `age` nor `timestamp` is accepted even though one of them is mandatory. The docstrings also describe the opposite of what the code checks. Use `is not None` checks and add object-level validation that exactly one of the two is present.

findings.title: Strict ChoiceField for report type rejects the whole batch with 422
findings.body: The old dataclass did not enforce the `Literal` type at runtime. `type = ChoiceField(choices=BROWSER_REPORT_TYPES)` now returns 422 for the entire request if any report has a type outside the eight hard-coded values, such as other Reporting API types browsers may send. The endpoint is explicitly meant to collect real-world data on what browsers send. One unknown report therefore drops every valid report in the same POST and discards the data the experiment is trying to observe. Consider accepting unknown types (tagging them as 'unknown' in the metric) and validating per report rather than failing the whole batch.

findings.title: Flagged TableWidgetVisualization renders hard-coded empty data
findings.body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, the table widget passes `columns={[]}` and `tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}}`. The real `result.data`, `result.meta`, loading state and custom renderers are all ignored. Any org with the flag on sees every dashboard table widget render as an empty grid. Either wire the real query results into the new component or do not ship the branch until it is ready.

findings.title: Query key omits organization slug
findings.body: The key is `['use-trace-item-attribute-keys', queryOptions]`, but `queryFn` fetches `/organizations/${organization.slug}/trace-items/attributes/` via `useGetTraceItemAttributeKeys`. The org slug is not part of the key. Switching organizations with otherwise identical page filters, project ids and item type can serve cached attributes from the wrong org. Include `organization.slug` in the key.

findings.title: get_environment_info does a per-issue event lookup and logs failures as info
findings.body: For each issue in the PR comment, `get_environment_info` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()`, which can hit Snuba and nodestore. That is up to five extra lookups, executed serially in the list comprehension while building the comment. Any exception is swallowed and logged at `info` under the name `no-environment`. Real failures such as Snuba errors are indistinguishable from 'issue has no environment' and will not alert. Consider batching or using data already available from the query, and log failures at a higher level.

findings.title: Default autofix automation tuning silently changed from 'low' to 'off'
findings.body: `DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT` and the `sentry:autofix_automation_tuning` project option default (src/sentry/projectoptions/defaults.py) both flip from `low` to `off`. Every project that never set the option changes behavior on deploy: automatic autofix on new issues stops. The change is unrelated to the PR's stated purpose (replay bulk delete) and has no description or migration plan. Confirm it is intended and split it out so it can be rolled out and reverted independently.

findings.title: 60s processing deadline may be too short for a 100-identity chunk
findings.body: `check_auth_identities` loops over up to `chunk_size=100` identities. Each one runs `check_single_auth_identity`, which can call the SSO provider's `refresh_identity` over the network. A 60s deadline can be exceeded when providers are slow. Those identities already had `last_synced` bumped in `check_auth` before scheduling, so a timed-out chunk is not rechecked until the next interval. The follow-up `check_auth.apply_async` at the end of the task also never runs for that chunk.

findings.title: None max_segment_id handling is not exercised by any test
findings.body: The new early return for `max_segment_id is None` in `_make_recording_filenames` is only reached through `test_run_bulk_replay_delete_job_completion`, which patches `delete_matched_rows`. The real filename generation and deletion therefore never runs with a null segment id. Add a direct unit test for `_make_recording_filenames` / `delete_matched_rows` with a `None` row so a regression would be caught.
